s: Land revenue, which was the chief source of income during the Mauryan period, was collected by which officer?
x: Sitadhyaksha was the head of agricultural land in the Mauryan empire, and he also dealt with land revenue levitation while Agronomoi were known as district officers. s: Which one of the following administrative structures in ascending order is correct?
x: In the Arthashastra the units are Sthaniya (800 villages), Dronamukha (400), Kharvatika (200) and Sangrahana (10), so the sequence Sthaniya, Dronamukha, Karvatika, Samgrahana is the correct order.

s: Rajjuka’s were:
o: Feudal Lords in the Gupta empire
x: ‘Rajjuka’ officials were mentioned in the edicts of Ashoka. Rajjukas were categories of officials in the rural areas, who worked as surveyors combined with judicial functions with assessment duties.

s: Ashokan inscriptions suggest that the 'Pradeshika', 'Rajuka' and 'Yukta' were important officers at the
x: A study of Ashoka’s inscriptions shows that Pradeshika, Rajuka, and Yukta–all three–were mainly “district-level officers” in the Mauryan administration. (1) Pradeshika is generally described as the chief administrator of the district (overall in charge). (2) Rajuka was a senior officer who played an important role in land measurement, tax assessment, and judicial functions. (3) Yukta is regarded as a revenue officer responsible for the treasury and accounts, and worked under the Pradeshika and the Rajuka.

s: Which one of the following officials was not a part of the Mauryan administration?

His 3rd edict mentioned three (3) officers which are mentioned below – YUKTA – These were the district officials there to collect revenue. RAJJUKA – Rajjuka was a category of officials in the rural area who worked as surveyors combined with judicial functions. PRADESHIKA – He was a top official of the division. He can be compared with the modern day commissioner. They used to perform judicial work also.

s: The head of a district (Ahara), the principal coordinator of the revenue and the officer in charge of general and military functions in his jurisdiction during Mauryan Empire was known as
x: Among the options only Rajuka is a Mauryan district officer, with survey, assessment and judicial powers. Krori, Faujdar and Chirastadar are later titles, so Rajuka is the best fit.

s: Which function of the present municipal administration has been continuous from the time of Mauryan period?

At present also, this work is done by municipal administration.

According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, which of the following are correct?

A. A person could be a slave as a result of a judicial punishment.

B. If a female slave bore her master a son, she was legally free.

C. If a son born to a female slave was fathered by her master, the son was entitled to the legal status of the master's son.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Which one of the following texts of ancient India allows divorce to a wife deserted by her husband?
x: The Arthashastra, attributed to Kautilya, contains comparatively pragmatic and secular legal provisions. It permits a woman to separate under certain circumstances, including when she has been deserted by her husband.

s: Which one of the following texts of ancient India allows divorce to a wife deserted by her husband?
x: Arthashastra allows the divorce and remarriage of a wife deserted by her husband. Divorce was prevalent in the Mauryan period. Wife had the right to divorce on the basis of the long abroad stay of her husband and being physically handicapped. Similarly, husband also had the right to leave his wife for being barren or adulteress.

s: In how many categories did Megasthenes divide the Indian Society?
x: Megasthenes divided Mauryan society into seven categories which are as follows : (1) Philosophers (2) Farmers (3) Herdsmen and hunter (4) Artisans and traders (5) Military (Soldier) (6) Overseers or Spies (7) Councillors and Assessors. Megasthenese does not mention slavery in India. According to him, no one could marry outside his caste, and no one could take to an occupation other than the one fixed for his caste according to the varna system.

s: Who stated that there were two types of philosophers: Brahmins and Shramanas?
x: The book "Indica" written by Megasthenes in Greek describes that Indian society was divided into seven main classes (philosophers, farmers, herdsmen, overseers, councillors, soldiers, and artisans). According to Megasthenes' account, Indian philosophers were divided into two groups: Brahmins and Shramanas. Brahmins: Those who believed that liberation (moksha) could be achieved through knowledge of the Brahman (supreme reality). Shramanas: Those who believed that liberation could be attained through ascetic practices (shrama).

Consider the following art and architectural forms:
I. Rock-cut elephant at Dhauli in Orissa
II. Yakshi figure from Didarganj near Patna
III. Great Stupa at Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh
IV. 80-pillared hall at Kumrahar near Patna
Which of the above art and architectural forms belong to the Mauryan period?
x: The Mauryan period (321-185 BCE) witnessed remarkable developments in architecture and sculpture. Emperor Ashoka promoted stone architecture and monumental art across the empire. Examples include the rock-cut elephant at Dhauli, the famous Didarganj Yakshi statue, the Great Stupa at Sanchi, and the 80- pillared hall at Kumrahar near Patna. These structures demonstrate Mauryan craftsmanship and imperial patronage.

s: With reference to the art and archaeological history of India, which one among the following was made earliest?
x: Option (b) is correct: Rock-cut Elephant at Dhauli (in Odisha) was made earliest among the other three. Situated on the banks of the River Daya, about 8 kilometers from Bhubaneswar, Dhauli was an important center of Buddhism. The site is renowned for the fourteen major Rock Edicts of Emperor Ashoka, dating back to the 3 rd century BCE. The finely carved half-sculpture of an elephant stands as a masterpiece of Mauryan art and serves as significant evidence of advances in sculptural techniques during that period. Option (a) is incorrect: Built in the 11 th century AD, the temple is a prime example of the Kalinga School of Temple Architecture. The deity Lingaraj is referred to as "Swayambhu", meaning self-originated Shivling. Built by King Jajati Keshari of Soma Vansh. Option (c) is incorrect: Rockcut monuments at Mahabalipuram were made during the 7 th century AD by the Pallavas. Option (d) is incorrect: Varaha Image at Udayagiri is located in Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh (not to be confused with Udayagiri-Khandagiri Caves in Odisha). Created in the early 5 th century AD under the patronage of Chandragupta II, it is famous for having numerous sculptures on the hill walls. The sculpture of Varaha, the Boar incarnation of Vishnu, is notable. The caves have one of the earliest Hindu sculptures. It also has caves dedicated to Shiva, Narasimha (half-lion, half-man), Narayana (resting Vishnu), and Skanda.

Which Buddhist text mentions Andhra Path?
x:
Vinayavatthu is one of the important Buddhist Pali texts that contains one of the earliest references to "Andhra Patha" (Andhrapatha). The term literally means "the country or region of the Andhras." The reference is historically significant because it confirms that the Andhra region had already emerged as a distinct geographical and cultural entity during the early Buddhist period. Such literary references, along with inscriptions and archaeological discoveries, help historians reconstruct the early history of Andhra before the rise of powerful dynasties like the Satavahanas. The mention of Andhrapatha in Buddhist literature also indicates the spread of Buddhism into the Andhra region through trade routes and monastic networks. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Earliest Buddhist reference to Andhrapatha – Vinayavatthu
• Importance – Early literary evidence for Andhra region

Jataka tales are used by historians as early literary evidence for regional names and geography in ancient India. This makes it a valuable source for tracing the antiquity of the term ' Andhra '.

Assaka (Asmaka) was one of the Sixteen Mahajanapadas mentioned in Buddhist literature. It was the only Mahajanapada located in the Deccan region. Its capital was Potali (Podana), which is identified with present-day Bodhan in Telangana. Assaka occupied an important position on the trade routes connecting North and South India. Later, this region came under the control of the Satavahanas. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).

s: In which one of the following regions was Dhanyakataka, which flourished as a prominent Buddhist centre under the Mahasanghikas, located?
x: The ancient Dhanyakataka in Andhra Pradesh was the capital of the later Satavahanas. It covers present-day Amaravati and Dharanikota. Buddhism had existed in this region even before the Mauryan period. The famous Buddhist sites of Amaravati and Dhanyakataka (Dharanikota) are associated with Buddha, as a birthplace of one of the previous births of Buddha & a preaching site of Buddha, respectively. During Emperor Ashoka's reign, Buddhism in Dhanyakataka gained prominence. The Amaravati Stupa (Mahachaitya) dates back to the Mauryan period, as confirmed by an Ashokan edict found at the site. The region was a stronghold of the Mahasanghika school. Options (b), (c), and (d) are incorrect: Gandhara: It is the present-day area of Northern Pakistan and Afghanistan. Kalinga: It is a historical region that encompassed modern-day Odisha. Magadha: This region is located in the Indo- Gangetic plains of eastern India and spans the modern state of Bihar.
